title: POC scoping: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private - Mistral Biotech
summary: Initial POC scoping focused on deployment mode decision (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Covered success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), workload sizing, benchmark plan, security requirements (SOC2/HIPAA/KMS/VPC), timeline and next steps. Redwood AE + SE to deliver pricing, security pack, and benchmark plan; customer to share sample traffic patterns and test data profile.
next_steps: Jordan Lee - send pricing tiers for Hosted / Dedicated / Private + seat/license notes - 2026-03-09
Priya Shah - share benchmark plan and scripts + required sample payloads - 2026-03-08
Mistral team - provide 48-hour sample traffic trace and example prompts (anonymized) - 2026-03-07
Schedule follow-up technical deep-dive to finalize infra constraints - week of 2026-03-15
action_items: Jordan Lee - compile SOC 2 / HIPAA attestation and security pack - due 2026-03-09
Priya Shah - prepare initial benchmark scripts (latency/throughput with 1k/5k qps patterns) - due 2026-03-08
Sofia Gomez - share model families and avg seq length distribution (tokens) + concurrency targets - due 2026-03-07
Marcus Li - confirm VPC/Firewall constraints and whether private peering required - due 2026-03-10
transcript: [00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer. We know you sent over the short brief. [00:12] Anika: Hi Jordan, Priya - thanks, we wanted to walk through what a POC would look like before procurement. High level the decision is whether hosted covers our needs or if we need dedicated or private. We're biotech so PHI-ish, HIPAA concerns come up. [00:28] Jordan: Totally. We'll talk simple criteria: latency, cost, throughput, data residency/compliance. Priya will run through sizing. [00:36] Priya: Quick intro then I'll jump into numbers - can you confirm expected QPS and payload sizes? [00:43] Sofia: Right now our user-facing app generates ~120 req/min at peak, about 2k requests per day average. Prompts vary, avg seq length ~400 tokens, worst-case 1,200 tokens for long context. Concurrency target is 20 concurrent sessions. [01:05] Priya: Ok that's helpful. So rough workload: 2k/day but spiky peaks. 20 concurrent, average response length ~350 tokens. Are you planning multi-turn KV cache usage? [01:16] Sofia: Yes for many flows we keep a short conversation history (we store context in our platform). We care about 95th/99th p99 latency. [01:25] Marcus: On security side our security team prefers no outbound data plane for some internal projects - might require VPC or on-prem. [01:32] Jordan: That pushes towards Private or Dedicated with VPC. Hosted can be ok if you can accept strong enclave options and SOC2/HIPAA attestation. We'll talk tradeoffs. [01:41] Priya: For the performance target - what do you want for latency? [01:43] Anika: For interactive clinician tools we'd like median <250ms token latency and p95 under 700ms for common prompts; p99 ideally <1.5s. But that's negotiable depending on model. [01:56] Priya: Good, that maps to CPU/GPU selection and batching. For average 350-token outputs you should budget tokens-per-second and consider KV cache to reduce repeated prefix computation. [02:07] Marcus: Cost is also material; we have a cap per month for API spend. We'll need guidance on expected token cost across modes. [02:15] Jordan: We'll include cost modeling in the pricing sheet. Hosted is lowest ops overhead and fastest to run a pilot. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost commitments; Private is when data residency or network isolation is non-negotiable. [02:27] Evan: Procurement question - how long is a POC and what does it cost? [02:31] Jordan: Typical POC is 4-8 weeks. Suggest: Week 1: onboarding + data + test harness; Week 2-3: hosted baseline + smoke benchmarks; Week 4: dedicated staging (if selected) + deeper benchmarks; Week 5-6: iterate, security review and handoff. Cost depends on committed capacity for dedicated. We'll propose a pilot credit for hosted. [02:49] Priya: On benchmarking - plan to run three phases: latency microbench (single request, 95th/99th measurements), throughput test (sustained QPS profile and burst patterns), and quality/regression checks on your eval prompt set. [03:01] Sofia: For quality checks we have 150 prompt/eval pairs and a few gold answers - can we run those in POC? [03:06] Priya: Yes please share them anonymized. We'll run them across model variants (base open model, quantized, and any Redwood-verified variants) and report difference in token usage and quality metrics. [03:18] Anika: On data protection - we need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO/SAML with SCIM. Also retention policy - we can't have persistent logs for PHI. [03:28] Jordan: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations on Private and Dedicated; on Hosted we have bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options and retention controls. We'll include SOC2 and HIPAA attestation docs. [03:38] Marcus: About network - do you support private peering or VPC endpoints? [03:41] Priya: Yes. Hosted has VPC peering options and Private deployments are fully customer-managed control plane and data plane. Dedicated sits in between: dedicated GPU pools with customer VPC connectivity. [03:51] Evan: Any performance delta between hosted and dedicated? [03:54] Priya: Hosted uses multi-tenant pools optimized for cost; dedicated gives you reserved capacity and more consistent p99s - usually lower jitter. Private on-prem can be tuned most aggressively but requires more ops work. [04:06] Jordan: Also model variants matter. Quantized models reduce GPU memory and cost but sometimes increase latency or slightly reduce quality. We'll include quantization recommendations per workload. [04:17] Anika: For benchmarks, what inputs do you need from us? [04:20] Priya: Sample prompts, 48-72h traffic trace (anonymized), target SLOs, and a small representative test dataset (150 eval pairs). Also note any restricted IPs for peering. [04:33] Sofia: We'll get those by Monday. [04:35] Jordan: Great. On success criteria, let's align: 1) Functional parity and acceptable quality on eval set (>= baseline model accuracy), 2) Latency SLOs: median <300ms, p95 <800ms, p99 <1.5s for typical prompts, 3) Cost within your target top-line budget (we'll model), 4) Security sign-off (SOC2/HIPAA or Private deployment if needed). [04:55] Marcus: That looks reasonable. For cost, we need an estimate for 100k tokens/day vs 1M tokens/day scenarios. [05:02] Jordan: We'll include both. Hosted per-token pricing; Dedicated will have reserved GPU pricing and lower per-token compute cost once amortized. [05:10] Priya: For benchmarks we'll run baseline on hosted first to get realistic p95/p99 numbers. If you need guaranteed capacity we'll scope a Dedicated pool size - e.g., 4 x A100-class GPU equivalent for your concurrency goals - but exact sizing depends on chosen model and batching. [05:27] Anika: Do you provide benchmark scripts we can run internally? [05:30] Priya: Yes, we'll share a JMeter-like harness and a python client that simulates KV caching, multi-turn, and payload sizes. [05:37] Evan: Procurement - if we move to Dedicated what's the minimum term? [05:40] Jordan: Typically monthly or annual reserved capacity. For pilots we can do a short-term reserved evaluation at a reduced commit to validate throughput. [05:47] Marcus: Any mention of competitors? Our infra team evaluated Anthropic and Self-hosted on SageMaker; we found costs higher for self-hosting but more control. [05:55] Jordan: Yep we expect that. We'll include a competitive note in the deck. [06:00] Priya: Quick note on metrics we will report: token-cost breakdown by prompt/response, per-route latency histograms, GPU utilization, and caching hit rates. [06:10] Sofia: Great, that visibility is important for us. [06:13] Anika: Last question - timeline if we start next week? [06:16] Jordan: Onboarding + hosted baseline in 2 weeks, initial benchmarks in weeks 2-3, decision on Dedicated/Private by week 4 based on results and security review. Full POC wrap by week 6. [06:27] Evan: Sounds good. [06:29] Jordan: Recap of next steps - we'll send pricing, SOC2/HIPAA pack, benchmark scripts, and a proposed POC schedule. You send sample prompts and traffic. Any other items? [06:40] Marcus: Nothing else, thanks. [06:42] Anika: Thanks all. [06:44] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kick-off. [06:48] [call ends]
